title: Lee et al. 2019 (ERP) — EEG dataset and OpenBMI toolbox for three BCI paradigms: an investigation into BCI illiteracy
description: EEG recordings from 54 healthy participants performing a 36-symbol ERP (P300) row-column speller task with face stimuli, across two sessions with offline training and online copy-spelling test phases. The dataset is part of a larger collection covering three BCI paradigms (ERP, motor imagery, SSVEP) and was used to investigate BCI illiteracy. It includes 62 EEG channels and 4 EMG channels sampled at 1000 Hz.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a BrainAmp amplifier and Ag/AgCl electrodes (62 channels, 1000 Hz, ground AFz, impedance below 10 kOhm) using OpenBMI software. Participants copy-spelled sentences by gazing at target characters and counting their flashes. Each character received 5 sequences of 12 flashes, with a 135 ms inter-stimulus interval and 215 ms stimulus onset asynchrony. The training phase used 33 characters and the test phase used 36 characters.
